## Proof

Let $\alpha_1, \ldots, \alpha_n$ be the $n$ distinct roots of $g$ in a splitting field (with $\alpha_1 = x$). Distinctness holds because $L/K$ is separable. Let $\sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_n$ be the $K$-embeddings of $L$ into an algebraic closure, labeled so that $\sigma_k(x) = \alpha_k$.

**Step 1: Express $M$ as a product.** For $0 \le i, j < n$,
$$M_{ij} = \operatorname{tr}_{L/K}(x^{i+j}) = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \sigma_k(x^{i+j}) = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \alpha_k^{i+j}.$$

Introduce the Vandermonde matrix $V \in \bar{K}^{n \times n}$ with entries $V_{ki} = \alpha_k^{i}$ (row $k = 1,\ldots,n$, column $i = 0,\ldots,n-1$). Then
$$(V^{\mathsf{T}}V)_{ij} = \sum_{k=1}^{n} V_{ki}V_{kj} = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \alpha_k^{i}\alpha_k^{j} = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \alpha_k^{i+j} = M_{ij}.$$
Hence $M = V^{\mathsf{T}}V$, and
$$\det(M) = \det(V)^2 = \left(\prod_{1 \le p < q \le n}(\alpha_q - \alpha_p)\right)^{\!2} = \prod_{p < q}(\alpha_q - \alpha_p)^2. \tag{1}$$

**Step 2: Relate $N_{L/K}(g'(x))$ to the same product.** Since $g(t) = \prod_{k=1}^{n}(t - \alpha_k)$, we have
$$g'(\alpha_k) = \prod_{\ell \ne k}(\alpha_k - \alpha_\ell).$$
The norm is the product over all conjugates:
$$N_{L/K}(g'(x)) = \prod_{k=1}^{n} g'(\alpha_k) = \prod_{k=1}^{n}\prod_{\ell \ne k}(\alpha_k - \alpha_\ell) = \prod_{k \ne \ell}(\alpha_k - \alpha_\ell).$$
Pairing each unordered pair $\{p,q\}$ with $p < q$, the two ordered factors $(\alpha_p - \alpha_q)$ and $(\alpha_q - \alpha_p)$ appear, giving
$$N_{L/K}(g'(x)) = \prod_{p < q}(\alpha_p - \alpha_q)(\alpha_q - \alpha_p) = \prod_{p < q}\bigl(-(\alpha_q - \alpha_p)^2\bigr) = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2}\prod_{p<q}(\alpha_q - \alpha_p)^2. \tag{2}$$

**Step 3: Combine.** Comparing (1) and (2),
$$N_{L/K}(g'(x)) = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2}\det(M),$$
so
$$\det(M) = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2}\, N_{L/K}(g'(x)).$$

**Sanity check ($n=2$, $g(t)=t^2-d$).** Here $M = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2d \end{pmatrix}$, so $\det(M)=4d$. Also $g'(x)=2x$ and $N_{L/K}(2x)=4\,N(x)=4(-d)=-4d$. The formula gives $(-1)^{1}(-4d)=4d$. ✓

Since $(-1)^{n(n-1)/2} \in \{+1,-1\}$, the determinant is expressed in the required form as

$$\boxed{\det(M) = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2}\, N_{L/K}(g'(x))}.$$
